results.title: Spotify Reports Third Quarter 2026 Earnings — Spotify
highlights:
In Q3 2026, we grew to 306 million Premium Subscribers, with growth across every region, and reached 788 million Monthly Active Users, while our Gross Margin and Operating Income came in ahead of expectations. We continued to add value for listeners, artists, creators, and authors by expanding Audiobooks to more than 180 markets by year end, bringing the Spotify Partner Program to 35 more markets, and launching Creator Memberships.

## Q3 2026 Earnings Results:

- - Premium Subscribers grew 9% Y/Y to 306 million
- Monthly Active Users (MAUs) rose by 11% Y/Y to 788 million
- Total Revenue increased 16% Y/Y (14% Y/Y constant currency*) to €5.0 billion
- Gross Margin improved by 136 bps Y/Y to 33.0%
- Operating Income reached €672 million

results.title: Spotify Earnings: Company Adding Users But Misses Slightly on Revenue - Bloomberg
results.author: Ashley Carman
highlights: The world’s biggest music streaming company reported that paying subscribers increased 2% in the third quarter to 306 million, slightly topping Wall Street’s estimates. Total monthly active users edged up 1% over the prior three-month period to reach 788 million.

results.title: Spotify (SPOT) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript | The Motley Fool
results.author: Motley Fool Transcribing
highlights:
- Revenue -- EUR 4,969 million, representing 14% growth on a constant currency basis driven by Premium and Ad-Supported gains.
- Premium Revenue -- EUR 4,487 million, increasing 15% on a constant currency basis due to subscriber growth and higher ARPU.
- Ad-Supported Revenue -- EUR 482 million, growing 9% on a constant currency basis led by automated biddable sales channels.
- Gross Margin -- 33%, expanding 136 basis points from the prior year reflecting improved cost structures in both business segments.
- Monthly Active Users (MAU) -- 788 million, an 11% increase reflecting 11 million net additions during the quarter.
- Premium Subscribers -- 306 million, growing 9% year over year with 6 million net additions.
- Premium ARPU -- EUR 4.95, increasing 7.5% on a constant currency basis driven by price increase benefits.
- Operating Income -- EUR 672 million, delivering an operating margin of 13.5%.
- Free Cash Flow -- EUR 735 million for the quarter, bringing the trailing 12-month total to EUR 3.2 billion.
- Share Repurchases -- 2.2 million shares for $1.1 billion year to date through Oct. 21, 2026.
- Cash Position -- EUR 9.9 billion in cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter with no debt other than lease liabilities.
- Social Charges -- EUR 22 million, which was EUR 13 million above forecast due to share price movements during the quarter.
- Headcount -- 7,284 full-time employees globally at the end of September.
- Q4 MAU Guidance -- 818 million, implying approximately 30 million net new users.
- Q4 Subscriber Guidance -- 316 million, representing approximately 10 million net additions.
- Q4 Revenue Guidance -- EUR 5.2 billion, including an expected 230 basis point foreign exchange tailwind.
- Q4 Gross Margin Guidance -- 33.8%, driven by favorability in both Premium and Ad-Supported segments.
- Q4 Operating Income Guidance -- EUR 820 million, including 6 million in social charges based on recent share price levels.
- Audiobook Expansion -- over 180 markets by year-end 2026, up from 22 markets previously.
- Ad-Supported Gross Margin -- 18.7%, up 105 basis points reflecting improved podcast cost structures and other costs of revenue.
- Premium Gross Margin -- 34.5%, up 130 basis points as revenue growth outpaced music and content costs.
- Capital Expenditures -- EUR 6 million, a decrease of EUR 17 million from the prior year.
- Biddable Advertising -- 40% of advertising revenue, contributing to the segment's growth acceleration.

...

- MAU: Monthly Active Users, a measure of the total number of unique users who interact with the platform each month.
- ARPU: Average Revenue Per User, calculated as total revenue divided by the average number of users in a given period.
- LTM: Last Twelve Months, a financial metric representing performance over the preceding 12-month period.
- IFRS: International Financial Reporting Standards, the accounting framework used by the company for financial reporting.
- Social Charges: Payroll taxes associated with employee salaries and benefits that fluctuate based on share price movements.
- eSDK: Embeddable Software Development Kit, a technology stack that allows Spotify to be integrated into third-party hardware and speakers.
- Large Taste Model: Spotify's proprietary AI-driven recommendation engine used to personalize content for listeners.
- Audiobooks+: A Spotify subscription add-on providing expanded access to audiobook titles.

results.title: Spotify Adds 11m Active Users In 3rd Quarter To Reach 788m • Channels Television
results.author: Emmanuel Monye
highlights:
Music streaming giant Spotify on Thursday said it had added 11 million monthly active users in the third quarter and had reached 788 million active users by the end of September, in line with the company’s forecast.

The uptick represented an 11-percent growth in users compared to a year earlier, Spotify said in a statement, adding that paying subscribers had grown by nine percent compared to a year earlier, reaching 306 million, just above the company’s forecasted 305 million.

results.title: Spotify Hits 306 Million Premium Subscribers, Will Thrive in ...
results.author: Georg Szalai
highlights:
Audio streaming giant Spotify posted a third-quarter revenue gain and ended September with 306 million paying premium subscribers, up from 300 million as of the end of June. The figure compares with the company’s 305 million forecast.

 Monthly active users (MAUs) grew to 788 million, up from 777 million in the previous quarter and in line with the firm’s forecast. Spotify had guided to slower MAU growth in the third quarter, pointing to changes to products in emerging countries to help the company better monetize its user bases. Revenue growth for the quarter came in at 16 percent, or 14 percent on a constant currency basis, to get the company to €5.0 billion ($5.6 billion), matching its forecast. Operating income hit €672 million ($754 million) in the third quarter, with management guidance having called for €670 million. The figure was up 15 percent despite a 26 percent operating expenses increase, “primarily driven by an increase in marketing alongside cloud and AI spend in support of growth initiatives.”
